title: A growing-end-preserving isometry that fails on two old distinctions
claim: There exists a finite positive-age stage of complete cheapest-count growth with a full bond-distance table isometry fixing every live junction pointwise such that no renaming extending it, even after loose-site re-pairing, preserves the next table.
standard_statement: In a connected multigraph with the exterior designated and parity equations given by ordinary vertex stars, the metric obtained from least common cocircuit sizes admits an edge permutation preserving the live stars and their observation. It need not extend after the next prescribed exterior split, even if the graph was itself obtained by such a split.
prior_work: The 1,746,752 qualifying HUNT-SHORTEN self-matchings and 36,060 carried matchings extended within their populations. A seven-site static failure lacked a positive-age history.
source_contribution: The explicit six-junction start was constructed during the associated experiment. This proof is written after that discovery. The proof supplies two lawful rounds and the cut argument from the axioms, with a fixed finite check independent of the search.

validation.status: V1. Standard stateful full-round engine, a separately authored exact round replay, verification by connected shores and minimal XOR supports, and an internal adversarial proof review. An external or separate program-level referee has not been counted.

completion_gate: Verify the two legal rounds, exact current equality under the named swap, fixed live supports and a decisive old-old successor inequality immune to any allowed repairs.
conclusion: There exists a positive-age stage and a specified isometry preserving the whole growing end with no isometry of the next table that extends it. The same fixed-old obstruction holds under allowed within-holder repairs.
evidence_class: Explicit finite mathematical countermodel, with an exact cut proof and independently checked literal history.
unrestricted_conjecture: Refuted for specified isometries on reachable stages.
